question: A charity tracked the total dollars in its emergency fund all month, starting at 234 dollars. A morning donation added 51 dollars. A dozen thank-you cards were mailed out that day, though that number has nothing to do with the fund total. An afternoon donation added 3 more dollars. A large emergency payout then removed 213 dollars from the fund. A grant then added 66 more dollars. A bank fee removed 84 dollars. Finally, a matching challenge multiplied the tracked fund by 6. How much money was in the emergency fund at the end of the month?

In the morning, Marcus had 109 points in a school reading challenge. By midday, he earned 32 more points finishing a chapter book. In the afternoon, he earned 32 more points for a book report. Later, a bonus quiz added 57 more points. By evening, 90 points were deducted for a late submission. A second deduction removed 12 more points. Finally, a school-wide bonus made his total nine times as large, putting him far ahead of his classmate Theo, who only had 200 points. How many points did Marcus end up with?

An artist starts with 87 pieces. He multiplies by 4 to scale for four galleries. He multiplies by 3 for a three-month exhibition. He divides by 2 to split into two collections. He adds 68 pieces from new creations. He multiplies by 4 to forecast four years. He multiplies by 3 for a three-location tour. How many pieces for the tour?

On Thursday morning a pet shop had 77 water bowls, and a delivery added 35 more before noon. At midday a second delivery doubled the number of bowls in the shop. During the afternoon 87 bowls were sold. In the evening head office supplied 8 bowls for every bowl left on the shelf. A customer then returned 32 bowls that were the wrong size. How many bowls does the shop have?

A farm with a dozen workers harvests 219 kilograms of potatoes from each plot. There are 6 plots in every field and 7 fields on the farm, and the harvest took 3 days. The crop is shared equally among 6 buyers, so the buyer Wren receives exactly as much as the buyer Pax. Wren then sells 1060 kilograms to a restaurant. How many kilograms does Wren have left?

A worker tracked tasks through morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 22 tasks, morning work completed 18 (4 tasks). Early afternoon removed another 2 through reassignment (2 tasks). Mid-afternoon brought 45 new tasks (47 tasks). Late afternoon additions brought 62 more (109 tasks). Evening cleanup removed 85 tasks. A colleague had 38 tasks separately. What was the final count?

In the morning, a food pantry has 188 cans of soup on its shelves. By midmorning, a donation brings in 73 more cans. Around noon, a school food drive adds 10 more cans. In the afternoon, a grocery store contributes 50 more cans. Later, a matching-donation event triples the entire stock. By evening, a final neighbor drops off 13 more cans. How many cans of soup does the pantry have by the end of the day?

A chess club records its games in whole hours rather than in minutes, and keeps all of its spare pieces in one box. On Monday morning the box held 18 pawns, but 3 were lost under the radiator and 2 more were chipped and thrown out. On Tuesday a member donated 66 pawns from old sets, and on Wednesday a school gave 51 more. The club meets in room 7 of the library. On Thursday a car-boot sale added 31 pawns to the box, and on Friday evening 92 pawns were given away to a beginners' class. How many pawns are in the box now?

A store manager tracked inventory. He began with 179 units. He removed 96 units for a clearance sale. He ordered a bulk shipment—7 times the removed amount. Then he subtracted 54 defective units. He multiplied the remaining stock by 4 for a mega-order. Then 55 units arrived as a surprise delivery. His assistant was comparing this to another location's stock. How many units are in the final inventory?

In the morning, a dance studio has 195 costumes hanging for a big recital. By midday, the costumes are split evenly into 5 racks for different age groups, and the story follows just one of those racks from here. In the afternoon, a donation of gently used outfits adds 43 more costumes to that rack. The studio's instructor, Maria, oversees this rack, while her rival across town, Wendy, has 70 costumes on her racks by comparison. That evening, a rush of last-minute registrations brings that rack's costume count to 2 times what it was. Right before the recital, 44 costumes on that rack are found damaged and pulled from use. How many costumes are on that rack now?

Dan collects 109 cans every day from the park, 33 cans from the beach, and 65 cans from the school, spending about half an hour at each place. The bins are emptied at 7. He does this for 3 days, and on the last day a neighbour gives him 65 cans. How many cans has Dan collected?

A community centre had 231 chairs at the start of the season. 22 chairs were scrapped as broken, and a hall closure sent 54 more chairs to the centre. A dozen of the chairs are the padded sort kept for the committee room. Every chair takes 5 minutes to set out, and the caretaker added up the setup minutes for all of them. He records this work in minutes even though his timesheet is filled in with hours. He saved 777 minutes by using a trolley, and his colleague Ana added 15 minutes of her own, although Ana worked fewer minutes overall than he did. How many minutes did the setup finally come to?

In the morning, a bakery has 84 croissants baked. By midmorning, 15 more come out of the oven. In the afternoon, a catering order triples the batch. By late afternoon, 63 more croissants are baked for a wedding order. By evening, a wholesale distributor multiplies the batch by 7, a delivery that takes 120 minutes, or two hours. Finally, 48 more croissants are baked for the next morning. How many croissants does the bakery have now?

Priyanka set out 123 paper cups at the halfway water station of a road race. Her fellow volunteer Noor brought 20 more cups from the gazebo, and the supply van dropped off 61 additional cups. The race itself is 42 kilometres long. A gust of wind blew 19 cups off the table and they had to be binned. Every cup on the table was used twice during the race, so 2 servings were poured from each one. Each serving was given 5 ice cubes, and the cooler still held 47 spare cubes that were counted in as well. How many ice cubes were counted at the station?

Yuki folded 58 paper cranes during the first week of the memorial project. She sent 30 of them to the children's hospital straight away. Her whole class then joined in, and the number of cranes she held tripled, becoming 3 times what she had. A friend from another school posted her 61 more cranes. When the display went up, volunteers folded a matching crane for every one Yuki had, so the display held twice as many. Each crane on the display was hung on a thread with 4 glass beads. How many beads were used on the display?

Hana had 134 origami cranes folded for a school display, while her classmate Ren had 90 cranes of his own. Hana gave away 133 cranes to decorate the gym for a big event. Her remaining cranes then tripled when her art teacher assigned a matching project. A folding marathon turned every crane into 7 cranes. A final showcase turned every crane into 7 more cranes. How many cranes did Hana have for the display after the final showcase?

Owen's recycling depot started the week with 198 crates of bottles, and his colleague Priya brought in 43 more, which was far fewer than Owen had collected on his own. Each of the depot's 4 lorries was then loaded with exactly that many crates. On the motorway 107 crates were damaged beyond use. A supermarket took 462 crates from the lorries, and a bottling plant collected another 154. How many crates were still on the lorries?

James and David managed items. Starting with 104 items, receiving added 24 (128 items). Damage removal removed 9 (119 items). Inventory adjustment removed 78 (41 items). Multiplication factor applied 8 times (328 items). Final distribution removed 210 items. Converting to dozens, this represented 9 dozen. What was final?

Mia had 19 charm bracelets in a display case, while her friend Nadia had 12 charms of her own. A craft fair trade turned every charm Mia had into 3 charms. A second trade turned each of those into 2 charms, a swap that took '60 minutes, or one hour' to finish. She then lost 53 charms when a display case broke. A final trade turned every remaining charm into 4 charms. A bonus round turned each of those into 4 more charms. How many charms did Mia have after the bonus round?

A vineyard had 70 crates of grapes ready at harvest. A bumper crop turned every crate into 3 crates. A second bumper crop turned each of those into 7 crates. A third bumper crop turned every crate into 5 crates. Finally, a large wine producer bought 2237 crates in one order. How many crates of grapes were left after the wine producer's order?

A model shop had 120 kits on the shelf and a supplier sent 37 more before the holidays. Every kit contains 7 painted figures. Customers bought 984 figures over the season. A cancelled order then put 53 figures back on the shelf. How many figures are on the shelf now?
A workshop had 86 items. They divided by 2. They removed 3. There was a dozen distractor items. They divided by 4. They added 35. They added 47. How many items?

A farmer harvests 90 baskets of apples. Then 25 baskets are set aside for a local cider mill. The rest are split evenly among 5 delivery vans, and only one van's load is tracked from here. That van picks up 15 more baskets from a second orchard. Finally, it picks up 50 more baskets, a stop that takes 45 minutes, well under the usual hour. How many baskets of apples does that van have now?

Tom's wallet was empty at the start of the week. He worked 6 days at a bakery and was paid 32 dollars each day, putting every dollar into the wallet. He found 5 dollars on the pavement and added them too. Then he spent 185 dollars from the wallet on a secondhand bike, and his grandmother tucked 9 dollars into it for his birthday. At the fair he fed everything in the wallet into a token machine that gives a token for every 3 dollars. How many tokens did Tom get?

A restaurant owner started the week with 224 kilograms of supplies. Monday she used 98 kilograms. Tuesday she used 99 more kilograms. She tripled her remaining stock as backup. Emergency supplies cost 37 kilograms. A wholesale delivery added 74 kilograms. A similar restaurant had 2 metric tons in separate items. How many kilograms did she have at the end?
